title: Security, Authorization, and Professional Boundaries
summary: Learn why defensive security requires authorization and scope.
objectives: Identify safe, authorized, and prohibited security activity.

vocab.def: Permission to perform an action on a resource.
The systems, data, and actions included in an authorized task.

sections.heading: Permission is part of the system
sections.body: Knowing how to perform an action does not authorize it. Security work must use explicit permission, defined scope, and safe escalation.

sections.heading: Defensive boundary
sections.body: This course uses synthetic systems and events. Students do not scan unauthorized networks, bypass access controls, steal credentials, exploit systems, deploy malware, or evade monitoring.

practice.prompt: A curious student sees an unfamiliar server. What is the safe response?
practice.answer: Do not access it; confirm scope and escalate through an authorized channel.

quiz.question: What makes a security action permitted?

reflectionPrompt: Why is permission separate from technical ability?
